description: Maps every Ziel-ID from PERFORMANCE_EXPECTATIONS.md §1.2 to exactly one primary benchmark case (1:1 mapping). Each entry carries a "status" field: "mapped" (direct 1:1 case), "proxy" (indirect proxy metric), "not_measurable" (no benchmark possible), or "gap" (benchmark missing, open subtask). "primary_case" is the canonical benchmark name for the SLO (mirrors primary_benchmark). "fallback_case" names an alternative benchmark when the primary is unavailable or hardware-gated. Used by CI gate (Check 7a) and tools/verify_benchmark_mapping.py. Wave2: v2.0 — primary_case/fallback_case added for replication/sharding/transaction modules.

GEO-3.note: Benchmark laeuft bei max n=100K; 1M-Extrapolation via O(log N) Komplexitaetsfit: ~138 us << 5 ms

R-1.label: Replikations-Lag P99 (SEMI_SYNC)
R-1.notes: WAL append throughput is a latency proxy; direct semi-sync lag requires a running replica cluster.

R-2.label: WAL-Shipping Throughput (Zstd L3)
R-2.notes: ReadFrom/1000 measures sequential WAL read rate; compression overhead is system-level.

R-3.label: Leader-Failover
R-3.notes: Initialization time is a lower-bound proxy. Direct failover benchmark (Raft leadership transfer) is a gap — see missing-cases §R-3-GAP.

R-4.label: HLC Conflict Detection
R-4.notes: WALEntry serialization measures per-write overhead as proxy for HLC stamping cost. Direct HLC benchmark is a gap — see §R-4-GAP.

R-5.label: CRDT Merge
R-5.notes: WALEntry deserialization is a structural proxy for CRDT merge cost. Direct CRDT benchmark is a gap — see §R-5-GAP.

R-6.label: WAL Replay (PITR, 100 GB)
R-6.notes: ReadFrom/1000 measures sequential WAL read throughput as a direct analog for PITR replay rate.

R-8.label: Cross-DC Lag ASYNC
R-8.notes: WAL read throughput is a proxy for cross-DC replication rate. Direct cross-DC lag requires a WAN simulation setup — see §R-8-GAP.

SH-1.label: Cross-Shard RPC P99 (LAN)
SH-1.notes: ScatterGather with 4 shards measures cross-shard round-trip latency directly.

SH-2.label: Connection-Pool Hit-Rate
SH-2.notes: ConsistentHash routing throughput is a proxy for connection-pool efficiency. Direct pool hit-rate measurement requires instrumented pool — see §SH-2-GAP.

SH-3.label: Percolator Commit P99 (10 Shards)
SH-3.notes: BroadcastHashJoin (10-shard) measures multi-shard coordination latency as proxy for Percolator commit. Direct 2PC Percolator bench is a gap — see §SH-3-GAP.

SH-4.label: Shard-Split Migration Downtime
SH-4.notes: Batch serialization throughput is a proxy for migration data-movement speed. Actual zero-downtime split requires a live-migration harness — see §SH-4-GAP.

SH-5.label: Write-Latenz während Migration
SH-5.notes: Batch serialization measures write overhead during data movement as a proxy. Direct concurrent-write-during-migration bench is a gap — see §SH-5-GAP.

SH-6.label: Rebalancer Decision Cycle
SH-6.notes: Deserialization throughput proxies for rebalancer decision processing. Direct decision-cycle bench needs scheduler mock — see §SH-6-GAP.

SH-7.label: Anti-Entropy Scan Throughput
SH-7.notes: Gossip message serialization proxies anti-entropy scan overhead. Direct NVMe anti-entropy bench needs storage backend integration — see §SH-7-GAP.

SH-8.label: GPU Reed-Solomon
SH-8.notes: GPU Reed-Solomon requires NVIDIA A10 hardware. CPU fallback uses scatter-gather bandwidth. GPU-runner required for production measurement — see §SH-8-GAP.

SH-9.label: Snapshot (1 GB Raft-State)
SH-9.notes: BroadcastHashJoin data-size throughput proxies snapshot serialization speed. Direct 1 GB Raft snapshot bench needs persistent storage mock — see §SH-9-GAP.

SH-10.label: Snapshot Kompressionsrate
SH-10.notes: Deserialization throughput proxies snapshot decompression. Direct ZSTD compression-ratio bench is a gap — see §SH-10-GAP.

SH-11.label: Replica Catch-up
SH-11.notes: Gossip serialization throughput proxies catch-up data transfer. Direct replica catch-up bench needs running replica pair — see §SH-11-GAP.

SH-12.label: Topology Change Propagation
SH-12.notes: FanoutSelection measures gossip fan-out decision speed as a proxy for topology propagation time. Full 100-node propagation test needs cluster mock — see §SH-12-GAP.

TX-1.label: OCC Commit P50
TX-1.notes: CommitLatency/1 (single-op transaction) measures P50 commit time directly.

TX-2.label: OCC Commit P99
TX-2.notes: CommitLatency/100 (100-op transaction) measures high-percentile commit latency directly.

TX-3.label: 2PC Throughput
TX-3.notes: WriteOnlyTransaction (10 writes, 4 threads) measures commit throughput; tps counter reports k/s directly.

TX-4.label: 2PC Latenz (5 Shards)
TX-4.notes: MixedTransaction (5 RMW ops) approximates 5-shard 2PC latency in-process. True cross-shard 2PC latency requires distributed harness — see §TX-4-GAP.

TX-5.label: SAGA Compensation Time
TX-5.notes: AbortTransaction measures rollback path as proxy for SAGA compensation. A dedicated SAGA bench with compensation DAG is a gap — see §TX-5-GAP.

TX-6.label: Deadlock Detection Overhead
TX-6.notes: ReadOnlyTransaction cost relative to mixed-transaction proxies deadlock-detector overhead delta. Direct overhead measurement via lock-graph cycle benchmark is a gap — see §TX-6-GAP.

TX-7.label: False Positive Rate
TX-7.notes: AbortTransaction abort-rate counter approximates false-positive conflicts under no-contention load. Controlled-contention false-positive bench is a gap — see §TX-7-GAP.

TX-8.label: Low-Contention Success Rate
TX-8.notes: OccOptimisticPut under low-contention workload measures success rate directly via commit vs. abort counters.

OC-3.notes: CPU path; BM_ImageEmbedding_Batch with arg 16. Reference value: 154 ms/image on i7-12700K (see plugins/image_analysis/onnx_clip/README.md). Benchmark instance: BM_ImageEmbedding_Batch/16.

OC-4.label: Text Encoding P95 (CPU)
OC-4.notes: CPU path; text/caption encoding latency. BM_ImageCaptioning covers the CLIP text-encoder path via mock plugin. Benchmark instance: BM_ImageCaptioning/224.

OC-5.notes: CPU path; measures plugin init + stats overhead independent of backend. Applies to both CPU and GPU execution paths.
